children: New Delhi, Nov. 15 -- Shares of Rolex Rings Limited have delivered impressive returns over the past few months. The auto ancillary stock ended last week with 6% gains. The Gujarat-headquartered company is likely to benefit from the 'Make in India' theme, according to IDBI Capital which sees nearly 17% upside potential in the stock.
Rolex Rings Limited shares ended 2.20% lower on Friday, as part of some correction witnessed after strong rally in the previous session.
With the settling down of the tariff uncertainty and improved demand outlook in both the business verticals, Rolex is likely to benefit from the 'Made in India' ecosystem.

The company reported strong set of numbers in the second quarter of financial year 2026-27. Its revenue from operations, EBITDA and profit after tax (PAT) increased by 43%, 72%, and 67% for the quarter on an annual basis.

"The revenue growth was majorly led by strong growth in the exports of auto components which grew by 90% YoY to Rs.1.29bn. The domestic bearings segment and the domestic auto components segment registered healthy growth of ~10% and ~30% respectively on YoY basis," highlighted the brokerage in its report.

IDBI Capital maintained a 'Buy' rating for the stock with a target price of Rs.241 per share. "We expect Rolex to be a strong beneficiary of the "Manufacture in India" theme. Utilisations are also set to move from ~65% in FY26 to ~70-72% in FY27.We maintain BUY with revised TP of Rs.241 at 23x FY28 expected earnings," read the brokerage report.

The auto ancillary stock closed 2.20% lower at Rs.213.25 per share on BSE with a market capitalisation of Rs.5,594.25 crore on Friday, November 13. Its share price value has surged 6% in one week, 30% in two weeks, 25% in one month, 44% in six months and around 91% in one year.
